newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to abolish 3 pct customs surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to abolish 3 pct customs surcharge.

text.p: Hungary's government on Thursday abolished the three percent customs surcharge from July 1, the government spokesman said.
"The government has decided to fully abolish the surcharge in line with its earlier commitments," Elemer Kiss told a news conference following the weekly government meeting.

The surcharge, originally slapped on imports at a rate of eight percent, was introduced in March 1995 as part of Hungary's economic austerity programme and has been gradually phased out beginning with the second half of last year.
It was aimed to lessen the pressure on the country's external position and together with other fiscal and monetary policies it helped Hungary reduce its budget and current account deficits.
